posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Look, I'm entirely with you when it comes to Marvel's double standards and marginalization regarding female characters. But I don't like Wanda and I find it weird how you excuse each and any of her actions and choices. Like when it comes to her joining Hyrda. You basically say "She had no choice, it was Tony Stark's fault!", thus stripping her of all agency. Did her parents' deaths play a huge role? Sure. Can her choice maybe somewhat be excused by the fact that she was a traumatized minor? Again, sure. But it doesn't change the fact that when she lost her parents, her first choice was to join a terrorist organisation. That's on her, not on Tony Stark or anyone else. She's simply not as moral a character as some others - don't tell me that, say, MCU Carol would have ever knowingly joined Hydra in a comparable situation! She turned against the Kree as soon as she realized that they'd tricked her and weren't the good guys! Even though she didn't have any particular attachment to the Skrulls or reason to care about their plight. Wanda wouldn't have turned against Ultron if he hadn't set his sights on Sokovia. She doesn't care if anyone but her and hers gets hurt, and very often contributes to their getting hurt. IMO this is different from characters like Tony Stark or Stephen Strange who, sure, have also made grievous and costly mistakes but at least had good intentions. Tony Stark created Ultron in order to protect the world - the entire world, even people he hadn't met or didn't particularly like, not just himself and his friends. I do think Wanda's moral alignment can best be described as "chaotic evil", though "stupid evil" might also work. You can usually count on her to make the most stupid and evil choice in any given situation. Lost your parents? Join a terrorist organisation. That didn't get you anywhere? Start working for a murderous robot. Your husband died? Mind-control an entire town so you can play happy families. Your children disappeared thanks to you using your powers? Don't go looking for them using your near-limitless powers (and maybe teaming up with the other powerful witch you know who's right here) - instead torture and murder a child, and murder countless adults just trying to protect her, so you can steal some other innocent's children and in the process create an incursion that would have claimed the lives of trillions. Comparing any of that to Clint's stint as Ronin, or to John Walker doing the government's dirty work, is just disingenious and IMO hurts your actual point that Marvel hold their female characters to a double standard and are all too happy to write them out. Especially given that Wanda's storyline gets way too much screen time already - between WandaVision, Dr Strange 2, Agatha All Along, and VisionQuest we have now had three series and a movie, all after Endgame, dedicated to her family. No other female character has had anywhere near as much focus on her story, and neither had Loki. For what it's worth I agree with you about Yelena. She's a somewhat similar character to Wanda in that, while she had a rough start in life that wasn't wholly her fault, she then continued making the most stupid and evil decisions possible. Red Guardian, Natasha, even Bucky once he got un-brainwashed, they all got out of the mercenary business. But Yelena continued happily murdering strangers for money while constantly whining that for some reason (I wonder why?) she didn't feel good about herself. And she gets far more screentime, focus, and sympathy than any other female character except for Wanda. Meanwhile the genuinely moral Carol got vilefied in The Marvels for not mothering Monica enough during a galaxy-wide crisis. Like I've said: double standards.

posts.title: [MOC] Frauenkirche Dresden
posts.text: Welcome to the final round, The lantern roof of the Frauenkirche is a timber construction, covered with copper sheet plating. Roof model assembly: still mounted on a baseplate 16 x 16 … … and taken apart: At first, I tried to build the roof shape with regular slopes, but the chamfered edges proved difficult. Later, I added curved slopes, cheese slopes and tiles to get the baroque appearance. Layer by layer, the roof is set onto the lantern – lots of SNOT and some offset. The golden cross on the top of the Frauenkirche is a donation from Great Britain. It was crafted by the son of one of the bomber pilots who had performed the air raid over Dresden in February 1945. What a great gesture of reconciliation! The historic cross had been found during the excavation of the debris in 1993. Restoration was not possible, due to severe damage and parts missing. It stands now inside the nave in memory of the countless casualties and horrors of modern warfare. After 3,5 years, my Frauenkirche MOC is completed at last. I like the shadow on the wall behind. Only a few mm clearance remains to the ceiling of my LEGO room (-: A small crowd is already waiting for the opening … Thank you all for your interest and patience, while following this thread. posts.title: [MOC] V-19E Super Torrent - Alternate Build of 75432 V-19 Torrent Starfighter
posts.text: What if the Republic had upgraded the V-19 Torrent into a hyperdrive equipped fighter designed to protect ARC-170 formations and give Jedi pilots greater independence? The V-19E Super Torrent retains the original fighter's wide central fuselage, but replaces its complicated folding wings with a fixed delta wing configuration. I wanted to give it a more streamlined, modern fighter profile, taking inspiration from the F-22 Raptor and the classic Buck Rogers starfighter. The raised, canted stabilisers add to the aggressive silhouette, while their position above the wings leaves room for the landing gear underneath. The integrated hyperdrive sits behind the cockpit, allowing the Super Torrent to travel through hyperspace independently without a carrier or separate hyperspace ring. I also moved the laser cannons forward to the front of the engine nacelles, along the wing roots. Placing them closer to the centreline gives the fighter a more naturally aligned forward firing arrangement. During the Clone Wars, the ARC-170 served as a long range heavy fighter for reconnaissance and combat missions. With three clone troopers aboard each aircraft, every loss meant not only the destruction of a valuable fighter, but also the loss of three trained crew members. A dedicated escort like the Super Torrent could have helped protect these valuable ships from enemy starfighters. Its integrated hyperdrive would also have made it useful for Jedi generals, allowing them to travel between systems without relying on the separate hyperspace rings used by many Republic Jedi starfighters. So why didn't the Republic build it? Perhaps the Republic leadership preferred mass producing smaller V-wing interceptors rather than investing in a dedicated escort fighter. The Super Torrent never entered widespread service, becoming one of those intriguing possibilities in an alternative history of the Clone Wars. Like the original donor set, the V-19E Super Torrent is solid and sturdy, making it suitable for both display and play. You can grab it and swoosh it through dogfights across the galaxy without worrying about it falling apart. This is an alternate build of the LEGO Star Wars V-19 Torrent Starfighter set. I hope you enjoy building it as much as I enjoyed designing it! Instructions are on Rebrickable and OpenStuds: https://reb.li/m/278197

I really think it's all down to Kyle Chandler. I saw somebody tweet out that it's like if you found RDJ to cast as iron man only to immediately put him in Endgame. If they'd only found him fifteen years ago... But yes, it is definitely bringing attention back to the corps and to Johns's and Morrison's work. Unfortunately as lego tightens their limits on what can be adapted into sets, the standard for how well the DCU has to do to get some real coverage seems to go up. Between skipping major MCU films and writing of star wars shows entirely, I think we're at the point where MOT has to make like $1.5bil ... and we also probably would need to swap from supergirls and peacemakers to batmans and wonder womans. I also wonder if the R-ratedness of the DCU factors into lego's calculations- by the end of this year 4 of our 6 DCU projects will have been TV-MA or R. There's really only one film that people watched and that tied into lego's target audience. We have recently seen that lego will bypass it for something like the Man games, but when we have a majority MA rated universe it does probably give them a bit of pause to make projects for the few PG-13 ones- like with MOT. (Also with MOT, is John even going to be Green Lantern? They have to give him some sort of costume, but will it be green? Will it have the symbol?) I would be happy to see a space-based GLC movie- my idea for the lanterns show way back when was Hal/John/Guy getting brought to Oa for training- and focusing on the larger corps would be a good way to sidestep the lack of Hal and whatever's going on with John. I also do think Guy has some popularity, and in another sort of sidestep thinking making Guy the main hero does work. His abrasiveness usually makes him a side/ensemble character but everyone in this verse is pretty caustic-tongued, and at the end of the day Guy legitimately is a very heroic person. You throw in a bit at the start to show what "gym teacher" actually consisted of and you'd have the audience 100% on his side. posts.title: 1:10 Scale Diesel Electric Locomotive
posts.text: Track bricks arrived! Full disclosure, I gave in to temptation, their are Alt brick 2x8 tiles and 1/2 plate 1 x 4 inverted tiles on the anti stud side of the rail head but the purist solution works just fine too. When we last left off from the wheelsets I was waiting for some brick hinge pivot pins at 5.6mm diameter for more bearing experiments and an attempt to create a bearing in a 68325 round brick with recessed centre which would allow me to put the outer races of the suspension tube bearing on the tube because that's how they look to be rather than how I have them on the wheel as they are now. Found some more images that confirm that my supposition was correct, but sadly couldn’t make it work satisfactorily, will have to leave the model reversed but functional unless another idea surfaces. Short clip showing how motor is hung from the axle: The hinge pins parts did make a passable bearing with 60208 31mm technic wheel which would be advantageous in the axle boxes as the reduced diameter hub would allow more clearance and a greater suspension travel but nowhere near the silky smooth perfection of the previous 68327 design so are not adopted. For now, that completes the wheelsets and traction motors at least for the time being, 6 wheelsets built and waiting for their chassis. So the chassis - a relatively simple rectangular frame with two additional cross members between wheelsets These locos use Co-Co bogies because they need to spread the loco weight across sufficient wheels to limit load on the rail and to lay down the power output but more wheels makes life difficult to keep them all bearing down hard on the track as soon as there is the slightest unevenness or grade change, obviously some sort of suspension is required to help matters. Even with suspension keeping six wheels evenly loaded is tricky, four wheels is much simpler, fortunately our steam predecessors had to find solutions to this too and for up to 10 wheels in some cases and those lessons were applied albeit in slightly modified manner. The common solution is to connect each pair of the wheel sets to the suspension elements via see saw beams (compensating beams or equalizing beams) with a wheel each end and the suspension point (spring) at the central pivot point this allows the beam to tilt to take up unevenness in the rail before the spring element has to be involved this reduces the travel in the actual spring suspension meaning the sprung mass of the loco makes smaller vertical motions and this in turn greatly decreases the impact of the loco on the rails and allows stiffer springs to be used (desirable for several other reasons). There's actually a heck of a lot more to it than that oversimplification but this is a Lego forum not a rail engineering one! But how do you put three wheels on a see saw? This is the neat bit, the middle set of wheels sits on the end of two beams but the spring pivot point is moved from the centre such that the leverage of the middle set is double that of the outer wheels so all wheels see the same net spring force. Six wheels now transfer their load through four nests of springs and the whole assembly looks like a much more stable and manageable four wheel setup to the gods of physics! This is about the fourth iteration of my compensating beam and it's still probably not strong enough and already overscale - we'll see!! So now we have side frames with three sets of guides (horns) for the axle boxes to move up and down, the axle boxes are connected at the bottom (in this case) to the compensating beams and the four sets of springs transfer the load of the loco down through the springs and out along the beams. This setup is known as the primary suspension and its chief function is to keep all the wheels in contact with the track whilst sharing the load as equally as possible. posts.text: In my head they've been $30 for years- yeah, jumping up the price in only a year or two is a little ridiculous. *coughs in battle pack* That's definitely an aspect of it, but I also feel like there was probably an element of the writer just not thinking through what they wrote. I imagine that Lucasfilm doesn't particularly care so long as they get their licensing fee, just because if they did, I would think they could exert some pressure on lego. Maybe that's what we need, for disney to flex some muscle and persuade lego to actually make some sets for something like MSL- the show got a great reception, but family-friendly TV is hard to promote nowadays with streaming replacing cable, and some tie-in lego sets would legitimately be strong marketing. It's a good choice at least- anything based on late bayverse just looks like actual magic to me in terms of how they get the transformation down. Hopefully they do cover Prime (and better than they did in legacy) in Studio Series, but even then the prices are just ridiculous- those new seekers are amazing, but I've resigned myself to not getting them because I'm not shelling out nearly $50 each for voyagers. Blokees is incredible and something that I always am glad to see the shelf space they have at retailers and number of IPs they work with expand. Their prices are generally a lot better than lego or hasbro and I do hope they're able to be threatening enough to get the other brands to stop jumping prices. I assume they'd "De-smart" anything in development, though I also assumed that they'd be doing that for the 2027 sets just based off the sales numbers and that didn't happen. If you can swallow buying used parts (which is generally fine so long as you make sure there aren't any damage notes, but every once in awhile you get someone with a very different idea of "good condition"), bricklink is almost always cheaper. (I'm sure shipping isn't quite the same, but I fairly often have that easy buy system say the cheapest cost overall is in a store in europe, so I imagine if anything it'd be cheaper for you sometimes.)
